newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Merrill Lynch to lower Hong Kong weighting.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch to lower Hong Kong weighting.

text.p: Merrill Lynch said on Wednesday it expects a 10-15 percent correction in Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index from recent highs and will reduce its weighting in Hong Kong in favour of South Korea and the Philippines.
"I am calling for a 10-15 percent correction from the recent highs," research director Adrian Faure told Reuters.

"I do think in the next three months -- or shorter than that, the next couple of months -- this market is going down certainly to 13,000 and possibly even down as low as 12,000. Fair value is at 13,000," he said.
The Hang Seng Index fell 18.19 points, or 0.13 percent, to 14,421.52 on Wednesday.
The index hit a record high of 15,020.96 on June 3.
"We will reduce our weighting slightly in Hong Kong. We will remain overweight but we will be taking some money out of Hong Kong in favour of (South) Korea and the Philippines," said Faure.
He said the Hang Seng Index's performance so far this year had been driven by three stocks -- HSBC Holdings Plc, China Light & Power Co Ltd and Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd.
"If you strip out the performance of those three stocks then this market would already today be at around 13,250, so it would be close to its fair value," said Faure.
As of Wednesday's close, the blue-chip index is up 970.07 points, or 7.21 percent, on the year.
"Obviously, it has been a very, very distorted market," said Faure.
